findings.what: The recent-success TILE and the list its count links to describe different populations — in the ordinary case, disjoint ones. The door counts Works whose COMMITTED RECEIPT instant falls in the seven MYT dates (`o.created_at >= v_from and o.created_at < v_to` over clara.operation_receipts, 0199:354). The drilldown it builds is `?status=completed&since=<from_date>&until=<to_date>`, and `clara.list_accounting_work` applies those fences to `w.created_at` on clara.accounting_work — the ADMISSION instant (0189:427-428). So (a) a Work admitted more than 7 days ago and posted this week is counted by the tile and excluded by the list, and (b) a Work admitted and settled `completed` this week with no committed receipt is excluded from the count (it drives `uncounted_completions`) yet is the only row the list returns. AC3's promise — the number opens the Work list already narrowed to exactly that population — is not met for this facet, and nothing on the tile discloses the difference. 0199's own header (:111-115) asserts the opposite: "the browser rebuilds EXACTLY these instants ... so the drilldown cannot mean a different week from the tile it came from" — true of the week, false of the subject.
findings.evidence: Measured on the from-scratch chain (rig650r 127.0.0.1:55609 / clara_650r, 194 migrations). Probe scratchpad/650rev/probe-a-drilldown.mjs built one client with W1 = posted today, accounting_work.created_at backdated 30 MYT days (session_replication_role=replica, the same shape client-work-pack.test.mjs:backdateReceipt uses) and W2 = completed today with no committed receipt. Output: window {from_date 2026-09-11, to_date 2026-09-17}; TILE {count 1, coverage partial, uncounted_completions 1, preview_ids [d8a28ce0…cfe9 = W1]}; DRILLDOWN via clara.list_accounting_work(p_client, p_status=>{completed}, p_since=>2026-09-11T00:00:00.000+08:00, p_until=>2026-09-18T00:00:00.000+08:00) = {rows 1, ids [55ff4526…3e96a = W2]}; VERDICT in_tile_not_in_list [W1], in_list_not_in_tile [W2] — zero overlap. The since/until instants are exactly what apps/web/lib/work/work-list.ts:111-112 sends (businessDayStart / businessDayEnd, lib/firm/activity.ts:258,272). By contrast the ACTIVE drilldown agrees exactly (probe-b-isolation.mjs: tile_count 2 = list_rows 2), so the defect is specific to the receipt-dated facet.
findings.fix: clara.list_accounting_work has no receipt-dated axis and recutting it is forbidden this wave (DECISIONS §1.3 lists no 0189 recut), so pick one on this branch: (1) drop `since`/`until` from the recent_success href (client-work-pack.ts:285-288 → `status: ["completed"]` only) and add one sentence to the tile saying the list is dated by when the Work was started, not when it posted — the list is then a superset, never a disjoint set; or (2) keep the dates and mark AC3's recent-success leg PARTIAL BY NAME in the report, filing the receipt-dated list axis as a follow-up. Either way add the missing red-first cell: in packages/db/tests/client-work-pack.test.mjs assert the pack's recent_success work ids against clara.list_accounting_work called with the exact arguments workAttentionHref spells (probe-a-drilldown.mjs is that cell).

findings.what: The only end-to-end proof of AC3 asserts the URL STRING and nothing about what that URL returns: the walk routes `list_accounting_work` to a hard-coded empty page, so every drilldown lands on an empty list and passes. No cell anywhere in the branch — db, unit or browser — compares a facet's count against the rows the list it links to actually returns. That is why 650-B1 shipped green through 12 db cells, 48 web cells and a 9-leg walk.
findings.evidence: apps/web/e2e/home-board-walk.spec.ts:110 `const EMPTY_WORK_PAGE = { rows: [], next_cursor: null, truncated: false };` and :134 `await page.route("**/rpc/list_accounting_work", (route) => json(route, EMPTY_WORK_PAGE));`. Grep of the branch for any assertion relating a facet count to list rows returns none: the db battery's 12 cells (packages/db/tests/client-work-pack.test.mjs) never call clara.list_accounting_work, and lib/work/client-work-pack.test.ts:230-246 asserts only that the href's dates rebuild the same instants.
findings.fix: Make the walk's `list_accounting_work` handler answer from the SAME fixture the pack mock is built from (return the WORK_PACK rows for `status=queued,running`, and the recent-success rows for the completed+dated query), so a drilldown that lands on a population the tile did not count reds the leg. Plus the db-side cell named in 650-B1's fix.

findings.what: The shipped migration header states a measurement that is wrong on attribution and that no artefact on the branch backs: "`ix_accounting_work_client (client_id, created_at desc)` (0178:367) serves the active scan ... both were measured on a rig cohort before this file was written". The planner does not use that index — RLS adds `firm_id = clara.jwt_firm()`, which makes `uq_accounting_work_intent (firm_id, client_id, intent_key)` the better prefix. The worker's own report concedes the sentence is backed by their post-hoc measurement rather than by anything the cut left (reports/650-final.md §Unverified bullet 4), but migrations are append-only, and the correction was not written anywhere on the branch — packages/db/README.md's new 0199 paragraph covers the consumer-first argument and the pin only.
findings.evidence: Independently re-measured on the ticket's own rig (127.0.0.1:55509 / clara_650, 1311 accounting_work rows, 77 operation_receipts, client with 102 active) as a bookkeeper with RLS in force, scratchpad/650rev/probe-c-explain.mjs: ACTIVE → `Bitmap Heap Scan on accounting_work` ← `Bitmap Index Scan on uq_accounting_work_intent` (Index Cond `firm_id = clara.jwt_firm() AND client_id = …`), exec 8.5 ms; RECENT_SUCCESS → `Index Scan using ix_operation_receipts_client` with the half-open MYT range as the Index Cond, exec 0.45 ms. Neither degraded to a sequential scan, so the CONCLUSION (no new index owed) holds; the attribution and the "measured before this file was written" clause do not. git diff origin/main...HEAD -- packages/db/README.md shows no correction.
findings.fix: Add two sentences to the 0199 paragraph in packages/db/README.md: the active facet is served by `uq_accounting_work_intent` (not `ix_accounting_work_client`) because forced RLS makes `(firm_id, client_id)` the leading prefix, with the plan and the cohort size; and state that the header's "measured before this file was written" clause is corrected by that later measurement. Do not edit 0199.

findings.what: `stopping` Work falls through every facet. The active predicate is `status in ('queued','running')`, so a Work whose cancellation is in flight — still executing, still holding a run — is neither "Running now", nor "Finished recently" (no receipt yet), nor "Waiting on a person". This matches the binding brief verbatim (brief-650.md line 8, DECISIONS §2 #650), so it is a ruling rather than a slip, but the board's own overlap sentence only warns that facets overlap; nothing tells a person a state exists that no tile carries.
findings.evidence: Nine-member roster at packages/db/migrations/0178_accounting_work_journal_successor.sql:306-307 (`queued, running, awaiting_input, stopping, completed, refused, failed, cancelled, expired`); the pack's two predicates at 0199:307 and 0199:315.
findings.fix: Record it as a named residual in reports/650-final.md (it is not in the current residual list, which names only D13), or include `stopping` in the active predicate and in WORK_ATTENTION_ACTIVE_STATUSES so the count and the drilldown move together — the latter is a brief change and needs the orchestrator.

findings.what: The needs-you tile inherits #629's active-client guard and turns it into a second assertion. `clara.list_review_queue`'s work_question arm joins `clara.clients ... and wqc.status='active'`, so on an `onboarding` or `archived` client the count is 0 and the tile prints "No Work is waiting on a person for this client right now." while the Work list the tile would link to still holds the rows. Inherited, not introduced — `ClientNeedsYou` already prints "Nothing is waiting on you for this client right now." from the same envelope — but #650 adds a second place where the same false negative is stated.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/650rev/probe-d-needsyou.mjs on rig650r: one client with one parked Work question — active → {chip_work_questions 1, list_awaiting_input_rows 1}; after `update clara.clients set status='archived'` → {chip_work_questions 0, list_awaiting_input_rows 1}. clients.status CHECK admits `active | archived | onboarding`. Guard at 0180:1077. Existing sentence at apps/web/messages/en.json:565.
findings.fix: Name it in reports/650-final.md beside the other measured residual (the chip's row-vs-Work count), so the wave knows two shipped sentences depend on that guard; a real fix belongs with whoever owns the review-queue splice.

findings.what: The needs-you count is viewer-floored but its drilldown is not. A viewer sees that tile populated (by design — that is the whole reason the number is not in the pack) and its count is rendered as a link into `/clients/:id/work?view=needs-you`, a list whose door floors at bookkeeper. The two pack tiles beside it say "Your role does not include this. Work records need a bookkeeper role…"; the one tile a viewer can read still offers a destination they will be refused at.
findings.evidence: The link is rendered for every facet whose count is > 0 (client-work-attention.tsx:118-124) and needsYouFacet is computed from the review-queue envelope, which the battery proves a viewer receives (packages/db/tests/client-work-pack.test.mjs, cell `p650.pack.floor_viewer`: the same viewer is refused CLR04 by the pack and still gets `counts.work_questions >= 1`). The list door's floor is the three predicates at 0189:344-347.
findings.fix: Render the needs-you count as plain text (not a Link) when the pack came back `denied`, which is the signal that this caller is below the Work floor — or keep the link and add the same one-line "Work records need a bookkeeper role" note under it.
